extraction.name: PIQA (Physical Interaction: Question Answering)
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, testing the ability of natural language understanding models to link text to a robust intuitive-physics model of the world.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com and asked to construct a physical goal, a valid solution, and an invalid permutation (trick) based on the instructions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was cleaned of stylistic artifacts and trivial examples using the AFLite algorithm, which discards instances whose feature representations are highly indicative of the target label.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to provide a physical goal, a valid solution, and a trick (invalid solution). Data was collected in batches and validated by other annotators for correctness. Examples with low agreement were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed, which sometimes included correct examples requiring expert-level knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset addresses reporting bias by prompting annotators with instructables to flatten the distribution of referenced objects and avoid prototypical solutions. It also uses AFLite to remove spurious annotation artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some examples marked as mistakes during development were actually correct but required a web search to verify. The dataset also removed examples requiring expert-level knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding via multiple choice question answering.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA.

description.evidence: Our dataset tests the ability of natural language understanding models to link text to a robust intuitive-physics model of the world.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: annotators were asked to glance at the instructions of an instructable and pull out or have it inspire them to construct two component tasks.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Our dataset is inspired by instructables.com, which provides users with instructions on how to build, craft, bake, or manipulate objects using everyday materials.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The dataset is further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm introduced in (Sakaguchi et al. 2020; Sap et al. 2019) which is an improvement on adversarial filtering... it discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: annotators are asked for 1. a physical goal, 2. a valid solution, and 3. a trick. The trick should sound reasonable, but be wrong often due to a subtle misunderstanding of preconditions or physics... Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples and validated by other annotators for correctness. Users will low agreement were de-qualed.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: In the HIT design the instructable provides inspiration... Annotator pay averaged >15$/hr according to both self-reporting on turkerview.com and our timing calculations.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data. This often meant that correct examples were removed that required expert level knowledge of a domain

rai:dataBiases.evidence: when thinking about how to achieve a goal, people most often are drawn to prototypical solutions and look for tools in the kitchen... To address this, and flatten the distribution of referenced objects (see Figure 5), we prompt the annotations with links to instructables... AFLite algorithm performs a systematic data bias reduction: it discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Manual inspection of the development errors show that some “mistakes” are actually correct but required a websearch to verify... correct examples were removed that required expert level knowledge of a domain (e.g. special woodworking terminology) which should not fall under the umbrella of “commonsense.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce a new dataset, PIQA , for benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding. The underlying task is multiple choice question answering
